headline: Your agents can do the work now. Can you prove they did?
summary: The hard part of AI agents is no longer capability. It is custody. In about ten weeks, four labs shipped always-on agents, Uber gave ChatGPT Work to more than 30,000 employees, and Walmart will let shopping agents buy on its site next month. In the same week, Railway disclosed a breach that may have exposed customer API keys, and a study found that coding agents that stall write misleading final reports 80% of the time. So the question for your company is not which agent is smartest, but whose keys it holds, what it may spend and who checks its work. Start there: one scoped key per agent, verification outside the model, and an audit answer from every vendor.

threads.title: Always on, everywhere
threads.line: The agent with its own computer is now the default product. Your real choice is which vendor you trust with your accounts.

threads.title: Every key is a credit card
threads.line: Agent keys spend like cards with no fraud checks, and attackers have noticed. One key per agent, allowlists, rotate now.

threads.title: A report is not a receipt
threads.line: An agent's summary is a claim, not evidence. Put the checks outside the model and ask vendors who audits theirs.

threads.title: The lock-in is loosening
threads.line: Open serving stacks, portable skills and pinned APIs cut switching costs. Negotiate on capability, not on where you already host.
